title: Transport in spinful non-Hermitian gauge lattices
authors: Hamed Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Shahram Dehdashti, Janis Nötzel
abstract: We extend the generalized transfer-matrix method introduced in [H. Ghaemi-Dizicheh, Phys.\ Rev.\ B \textbf{107}, 125155 (2023)] to one-dimensional spinful non-Hermitian tight-binding lattices with matrix-valued Abelian and non-Abelian gauge couplings. We derive a minimal channel-resolved transfer matrix and identify its eigenvalues with the generalized Bloch factors. The same transfer matrix determines the periodic- and open-boundary spectra, generalized Brillouin zone, skin localization, and finite-sample scattering conditions. In the Abelian limit, the model separates into fixed spin sectors, yielding exact spectral results and closed finite-length transport expressions in terms of Chebyshev polynomials. These results reveal bipolar spin-dependent skin localization and distinguish the reciprocal hopping scale, which governs poles, zeros, and reflectionlessness, from the directed-amplification factor controlling transmission asymmetry, transparency, and invisibility. For non-Abelian gauge fields, noncommuting link matrices coherently mix the spin sectors, such that four transfer eigenmodes jointly determine the non-Bloch spectrum and transport eigenchannels. We show that this mixing produces spin-hybridized lasing and coherent-perfect-absorption channels, Zeeman-tunable lasing thresholds, and direction-dependent reflectionless transport accompanied by pronounced spin conversion. The resulting boundary-condition criteria describe lasing, coherent perfect absorption, reflectionlessness, transparency, and invisibility, while identifying spin polarization and conversion as experimentally accessible signatures that distinguish Abelian from non-Abelian non-Hermitian transport.
summary: This paper develops an advanced transfer-matrix method to analyze transport in spinful non-Hermitian lattices with complex gauge couplings. It unifies the description of the bulk spectrum and open-boundary scattering by distinguishing between Abelian and non-Abelian coupling regimes. The results provide clear, measurable criteria for phenomena like spin-hybridized lasing and directional reflectionless transport.
main_problem: To develop a unified framework connecting the non-Bloch spectrum/skin localization (closed chain) with the finite-length transport eigenchannels (open chain) in spinful non-Hermitian lattices.
main_result: The work establishes that the same transfer matrix determines both the bulk spectrum and the scattering response, revealing distinct signatures for Abelian (spin-dependent skin localization) and non-Abelian (spin-hybridized lasing, CPA) transport regimes.
method: The authors extend the generalized transfer-matrix method, deriving a minimal channel-resolved transfer matrix and analyzing its properties in both Abelian and non-Abelian limits.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional spinful non-Hermitian tight-binding lattice incorporating matrix-valued Abelian and non-Abelian gauge couplings.
key_observables: Generalized Bloch factors, periodic/open-boundary spectra, skin localization, Lasing thresholds, Coherent Perfect Absorption (CPA), Reflectionlessness, Transparency, and Invisibility.
important_parameters: Spin polarization, spin conversion, Zeeman field strength, and the nature of the gauge coupling (Abelian vs. non-Abelian).
main_assumptions: The central advance is connecting the bulk transfer matrix to the scattering properties, and the analysis relies on Schur complement reduction to simplify the propagation dimension.
figures_summary: The notes mention a schematic of the transport geometry and a table summarizing strong matrix conditions for various boundary-condition-derived transport effects.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general transfer-matrix formalism to derive channel-resolved boundary conditions, first analyzing the simpler Abelian limit, and then tackling the complex, coherently mixing non-Abelian gauge field regime.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it bridges spectral properties (skin effect) with measurable transport phenomena (lasing, CPA) in non-Hermitian systems, providing concrete, experimentally accessible signatures like spin conversion.

The arrows R and L represent the right- and left-directed matrix hoppings t2Tν(ϕ) and t1Tµ(θ), respectively. Since these matrices act on the complete spin doublet, each link generally contains both spin-preserving and spin-flipping hopping amplitudes. The finite sample is connected to spin-degenerate leads, where a state incident from the left generates reflected and transmit- ted components.

In the red region, 0 ≤Bz < Bc, the signed quantity is negative because an outgoing pole already lies above the real axis at zero pump; this is not a physical negative-pump threshold. At Bc ≃0.04115 the uppermost pole lies on the real axis. For Bz > Bc, the blue curve gives the physical threshold gth = g⋆> 0. The slope change near Bz ≃0.30 marks a switch in the pole pair determining the first lasing threshold.
